properties.notes: Sheet 2-SE-4D (Aug 1983, after the photo). A closed heavy solid outline, long axis bearing about 149 deg, about 1.4 x 6.5 m on the heavy line's centre (1.9 m across its outer edges), with a thinner line drawn about 0.3 m inside it all round: this is the 'double line'. FP063 is about 1.0 m to its west and FP064 about 1.4 m to its east; it touches neither. My reading: a narrow structure with its own walls (solid outline = permanent), such as a narrow store, or a tank or trough whose thick walls are drawn double; NOT a free-standing wall (the legend has its own symbol for that, a line with dots) and NOT a covered passage (it is closed at both ends and joins neither shed). Regular stipple dots fill the gaps between FP063, this outline and FP064 and its inside; their meaning is not in the legend crops. Photo, with the outline moved into the photo frame: a very bright strip about 1.2 m wide and 5 m long (grey about 215) on the same axis overlaps only its east half and runs about 0.6 m past its east side; its west half is mid-grey like the ground around, with a dark line just outside its west side. The bright strip may be this structure's roof with a local misfit of about 0.6 m, or a paved strip in the gap; cannot tell. nosnap: snapping went to the thin inner line and the stipple dots (corners moved 0.55-0.64 m, area 9 -> 3.6 m2); corners kept on the heavy line's centre, read on sheet profiles across and along it. | reader: Sheet: narrow closed rectangle (~1.3 x 7.4 m) in solid line, parallel to and ~1.5-2 m SW of the cyan building, with a regular dot stipple over it and the gap (stipple meaning unknown; not a dotted wall line); magenta follows the inner edge of the drawn lines to ~0.2 m, no overlap with cyan. Photo: at the outline a mid-grey band with a sharp dark line on its SW edge; the very bright strip of similar width lies ~1-1.5 m NE of it (over the stippled gap, hugging the cyan building, and continuing as an L along that building's SE side), so it reads as the neighbour's lit wall/apron rather than this structure. Could be a low shed, trough or drain; not confirmed. | reader: Sheet 2-SE-4D (Aug 1983, after the photo). Narrow rectangle with a solid outline (about 1.4 x 6.5 m) in the gap between two buildings. Magenta on the drawn lines to under 0.2 m. The scattered dot stipple also covers the gap and the neighbouring building, so it is scan texture, not a wall symbol. Clear of the cyan footprints (about 1 m to the SW, 1.3 m to the NE). Photo: the outline area is mid-grey, with a thin dark line along its SW side. A very bright strip about 1 m wide fills the gap NE of it, and no shadow of a tall structure falls on that strip. The south third lies in a dark band. Could be a low structure or a path; cannot tell.

Both readers of p004 saw a real roof and called it the same building as FP167; the first-round reader of FP167 saw the same. The building keeps the id FP167; its Dec 1982 outline is the roof, its 1981 outline is kept as sheet_outline_1981 | light-grey roof north of and overlapping the sheet hut FP167 | Uniform light-grey roof with straight edges, rotated about 4 deg clockwise; a bright strip about 0.7 m wide along its south edge (eave or gutter, included); dark shadow and tree along the north side. It overlaps the north half of FP167 (the sheet TS square, Jan 1981): the roof south edge is at N 840629.0-840629.4 and the FP167 north edge at about N 840632, so about 2.5-3 m of overlap. The roof has the same E-W width and position as FP167 but lies 1.5-3 m further north even after allowing for the 0.85 m sheet offset, so it is either FP167 rebuilt or extended northward after the survey, or a separate roof built over its north part. A reviewer should decide whether this replaces FP167 or is added beside it; it is not part of FP167 as drawn.
